comments:
"I want to thank you for applying for admission to the Graduate Program of the Department of Sociology and the Department of Community and Environmental Sociology at UW-Madison for Fall 2026. The Graduate Admissions and Awards Committee has made its final decisions, and I am sorry to report that we are unable to offer you admission to the program.
The committee thoroughly examines each application and considers a wide range of factors when selecting applicants, including academic record, transcripts, statement of purpose and applicant’s goals, letters of reference, writing sample, previous research experience, fit with our program, and the probability of each candidate`s success in the type of program we offer. comments:
I received an email from the Director of the Doctoral Program congratulating me on my admission and providing the letter of admission with the full details of my offer. An additional email from the graduate school with full details is supposed to follow shortly. I received full funding for five years for 12 month/year including a minimum stipend of $43k annually and was also given details about additional funding resources through the program and graduate school.
A few more details to share: prior to applying, I did not contact my intended advisors to talk about applying. Also, I did not receive an interview request prior to receiving admission. I was accepted without any direct contact between myself and my intended advisors through my whole process of application.
I have a year of previous ethnographic fieldwork, over a decade of life experience in the context I want to work in, years of professional experience in social research methods, two master's degrees with GPAs of 3.6, and some slight professional connections to my intended advisors (mostly through my past professors who are acquaintances with them). Strong “fit” with my intended advisors and a good SOP was key, I think, in my admission.

With best wishes

comments: I had had an interview on Monday, 2.2.26 , and received an informal email of acceptance on Wednesday 4.2.26. Ami, senior undergrad at T15 (if that's even a term ppl use), have apparently very strong writing sample/original research, no publications, some teaching experience, had a couple of okay/good interviews at two other good schools, but tbh their programs put such an emphasis on practically ancient/disconnected from present-day literature and traditional approaches that I am glad things worked out the way they did. The professors at this institution showed such enthusiasm for me and my work that it is without a doubt the right fit; Find you a school that is excited about you as you are it. I think program fit is the most important part, I'm realizing. I haven't gotten rejections / any kind of decision from other places yet, but I have already informally accepted U-Mich and will most definitely be attending there. I found that you have to find the program that really fits your needs and goals, and then things tend to fall into place. I never thought they would. Best of luck to everyone.

comments:
I am pleased to invite you to attend our University of Washington Bioengineering Department Visit from March 12-14th in Seattle, WA.

 

During your visit, you will have the opportunity to meet with our faculty and graduate students, tour UW laboratories and campus facilities, and learn more about life in Seattle and the Pacific Northwest.

 

For candidates residing outside the Seattle metropolitan area, the Department will cover the cost of a round-trip economy flight, provide a $400 lodging stipend, and cover most meals during your visit. Please note that candidates are responsible for any airfare or seat upgrades, luggage fees, and transportation to and from their home/departure airport. Local candidates may apply for a $150 transportation stipend to help offset mileage, parking, or related expenses.

 

Unfortunately, the department is not able to host candidates at an alternative time.

 

Our goal is to offer funding packages to all accepted PhD students. To ensure we can offer the most comprehensive and accurate funding packages, admission and funding offers will be decided shortly after this visit event. waitlist for the MFA Program in Creative Writing at The Ohio State University. All of us on the faculty here
greatly admire your work and would be delighted to have you with us next year should a spot open. 

The truth is, determining “who gets in” versus “who gets waitlisted” once we have agreed on a group of writers
we want to admit is always ridiculously difficult. This is an inexact business (and of course it’s not a “business”
at all), and ours is a very small program by design. Please be aware that you are among a distinguished group of
writers who received enthusiastic “yes” votes from every one of the relevant faculty. 

I can promise you that the very latest you will hear from us about your admission will be one week after April
15, which is the date by which all admitted students must either decline or accept our offer. It’s very possible
that you will hear from us sooner, but I wouldn’t count on that, as many people wait until the last possible
minute to say yes or no. All I can tell you for sure is that as soon as we know how many offers have been
accepted, I will contact you one way or the other.
